blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Addresses with non-ASCII characters are logged in clear) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.recommendation: The pattern only accepts ASCII letters on both sides of the `@`. For `logInfo("signup", { email: "josé@example.com" })` the character right before `@` is `é`, so no match starts anywhere and the full address goes to the 90-day hosting logs; `ada@exämple.com` fails the same way on the domain side. This breaks the proposal's promise ("masks every e-mail address") and GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) / Art. 25. Match Unicode letters (`\p{L}\p{N}` with the `u` flag) in the local part and the domain, and add tests for an internationalised local part and domain.
findings.title: Addresses with non-ASCII characters are logged in clear

findings.recommendation: The pattern requires a literal `@`. A logged request path such as `logInfo("GET /reset?email=ada%40example.org")` contains the address percent-encoded (`%40`), so `maskEmails` leaves it untouched and the full address reaches the logs (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)). Also match `%40` as the separator (case-insensitive), or decode before masking, and cover it with a test.
findings.title: URL-encoded addresses are not masked

findings.recommendation: Only values go through `maskEmails`; keys are copied as is. A caller that keys fields by user, e.g. `logInfo("quota", { [user.email]: count })`, writes `{"ada.lovelace@example.org":3}` to the logs, against the docblock "never writes a full e-mail address" and the proposal's "the message and the fields". Mask the key too: `safe[maskEmails(key)] = …`.
findings.title: Field names are written to the log without masking

findings.recommendation: `a***@example.org` is still personal data when the domain is personal or small (e.g. `j***@janedoe.fr`), and it stays 90 days at the hosting provider. Whether that residue is acceptable depends on the domains the customers use, which the reviewer could not see. A question for the team: if the first letter and domain are not needed for debugging, replace the whole address with a fixed token or a keyed hash (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 25).
findings.title: The masked form keeps the first letter and the full domain
